summary: Validated the teardown detach/branch-delete guard against the real bin/fm-teardown.sh in disposable fixtures, including a pre-fix reproduction and the orca code path. The fix protects an enclosing checkout's main branch, preserves normal linked-worktree cleanup, and the new regression test runs green in the pr-forge family. No issues found.
tested: `bash tests/fm-teardown-detach-guard.test.sh` (new regression test, all 5 cases pass)
Live driver `/home/justin/.no-mistakes/evidence/01M45H8V5TGC73BJZH6G3WJT4E/live-scenarios-driver.sh` (8 scenarios against the real teardown + base-commit teardown + orca backend path)
testing_summary: Drove the real bin/fm-teardown.sh task --force in isolated throwaway FM_HOME fixtures with fake external tools. Scenario 1 (task worktree is a plain directory inside a primary checkout) kept outer main and HEAD on main and printed the one-line 'not detaching or deleting a branch' warning; scenario 2 ran the same fixture against the base-commit teardown and reproduced the incident exactly (HEAD detached, refs/heads/main deleted). Scenario 3 (primary checkout itself as worktree) and scenario 4 (linked worktree checked out on the default branch) both kept main with the warning. Scenario 5 (normal linked worktree on fm/task-x1) still detached and deleted the fm/ branch with no warning, so normal cleanup is intact. Scenario 6/6b confirmed tests/lib.sh GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES keeps fixture git discovery contained, while the pre-fix lib.sh escaped into the enclosing checkout. Scenario 7 drove the orca backend block (hand-built orca CLI stub, since orca is not installed) and it reached the shared guard, skipped the detach/delete, and kept main. The new regression test passes directly and through bin/fm-test-run.sh (family=pr-forge). No failures.
